clue.text: One of us dropping couple in centre of resort

indicators.note: dropping the couple in the centre tells us to remove the middle pair of letters from the resort's name

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A Brit drops a pair of something in the middle of a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON has eight letters, so its central couple is G and H; take them out. 'One of us' works because the setter and Guardian readers are British.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton is a British person, so from a British setter's viewpoint one of our own people.

clue.text: Produce metallic sound as band

definitions.meaning: to make a bell-like clang, as a struck bell or phone does
a circular strip, such as one worn on the finger

explanation.surface: A brass band producing a clanging metallic noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell's peal is its sounding, and a hoop or circlet worn on a finger is also called this.

clue.text: A couple of hunters, perhaps, who cheat?

definitions.meaning: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover, i.e. a timer, so two of them are a pair of timepieces
people who are unfaithful to a partner by seeing someone else in secret

explanation.surface: A pair of huntsmen who turn out to be cheats.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithful lovers are said to two-time a partner, and two timepieces are literally a pair of timers.

clue.text: Deny any wrong, for example

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of any are put out of order

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, as in 'fruit, say, apples'

explanation.surface: Denying any wrongdoing, as an example of innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal, and 'for example' is the word used to introduce an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To naysay is to refuse or contradict, so it is a synonym for deny.

clue.text: He and I fail to provide part of engine

parts.note: he refers to a male, a man
a business that fails is said to fold

explanation.surface: Two people failing to supply a component for a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' gives MAN, as a male person, and 'to provide' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifold is the branched pipe in a car engine that carries intake air or exhaust gases.

clue.text: Pleasant listening — such as 1, 7, 13, 18, 21 and 26, say?

parts.note: each of those answers, when spoken, sounds like the name of a composer, so they are composers to the ear

explanation.surface: Something nice to hear, illustrated by a list of other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: BRITON, FRANC, VILE, LIST, BACKS and HANDLE sound like Britten, Franck, Weill, Liszt, Bach's and Handel: composers' music heard rather than seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes news or sounds that are welcome and delightful to hear.

clue.text: Able to figure nature out without me

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the scrambled letters surround the other word
out signals that the letters of nature are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone can work things out naturally even when the speaker is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not 'lacking', which is the reading the surface invites.
explanation.definitionFit: Being numerate means being competent with numbers, able to do sums or figure things out.

clue.text: Dictator, none the less, abandoned European currency

indicators.note: the less means minus, so the zero comes off the dictator's name

parts.note: General Franco was the dictator of Spain
none is nothing, a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dictator, despite everything, gave up a European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like 'nevertheless'; it is O (nothing) subtracted from FRANCO.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and Belgium until the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Flexibility of wings, say, wrapped around seabirds

indicators.note: wrapped around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: wings are examples of limbs
erns or ernes are sea eagles

explanation.surface: Seabirds' flexible wings folded around their bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped around' is the container signal; erns (or ernes) are sea eagles, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Limberness is suppleness, the quality of bending easily, so it means flexibility.

clue.text: Chap writing War and Peace, for example

parts.note: Antony is a man's name
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A man writing Tolstoy's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Tolstoy's novel is the obvious reading, but the definition is the two words war and peace, which are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: War and peace are words of opposite meaning, so the pair are examples of opposites.

clue.text: Bad atmosphere in which mother keeps one apart from son

indicators.note: apart from says the son letter is kept within mother too, but separated from the numeral
keeps means holds inside, so the numeral goes within the word for mother

parts.note: mama is an informal word for mother
one is the Roman numeral I
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother keeps her child away from her son in a tense household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts I inside MAMA (MIAMA), and 'apart from' places S in a different gap: M-I-A-S-M-A. 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant or unhealthy air or a heavy, oppressive feeling.

clue.text: Flaws in church's positions, by popular account

indicators.note: by popular account means as people commonly say it, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: curacies are the posts held by curates, church positions, so this is spoken as 'in curacies'

explanation.surface: Flaws in the Church's official stance, according to common opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'in curacies' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaccuracies are errors or mistakes, so they are flaws.

clue.text: Person with convictions? Yes and no

definitions.text: Person with convictions? Yes and no

parts.words: Person with convictions? Yes and no
parts.note: read literally, one who serves a sentence in prison has convictions; but the word also means an opportunist who has no principles

explanation.surface: Someone who both has and lacks firm beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an opportunist who changes views to suit those in power, and literally a prisoner serving time.

clue.text: At the core, privileges seen as rotten

indicators.note: at the core points to letters taken from the middle of the next word

explanation.surface: Privileges, deep down, are seen as corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile means foul or wretched, so it is a synonym for rotten.

clue.text: Dismissed second player on side — using this?

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a wing is a player on one flank of a team in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A cricketer dismissed by a delivery that swung away.
explanation.walkthrough: An outswing is a cricket delivery that swerves away from the batter; the definition asks what the batter was dismissed with.
explanation.definitionFit: An outswinging delivery is a common way of getting a batsman caught behind, so the dismissal used it.

clue.text: Present knight after thriving king celebrated

indicators.note: after says the first pair of pieces follows the second pair

parts.note: a thriving person is doing well
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the present moment is now
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A celebrated knight gives a gift after a prosperous king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift or a verb; it is NOW, the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-known means famous, so it is a synonym for celebrated.

clue.text: Having a specific position and special duties over a short time

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the reworked word goes around the other pieces
special suggests the letters of duties are arranged in a particular new way

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An official assigned special duties for a brief period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' turns DUTIES into SITUED, and 'over' puts that around A and T: SITU-AT-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated is located in a particular place, so it has a definite position.

clue.text: Idiot breaking rule put in new post

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the other word open to go inside it

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their rule
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool who breaks the rules is moved to another job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the container signal: the fool splits the word for rule open.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign someone is to transfer them to a different job or role.

clue.text: Lean over the edge

definitions.meaning: a ship that tilts to one side does this
the border or selvage of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone leaning out over a precipice.
explanation.definitionFit: A listing ship leans to one side, and a list is also a strip along the edge of fabric.

clue.text: Stick unusually hard, as tacky stuff

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of stick are placed in an uncommon order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Glue that is unusually firm, like cheap sticky stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' is the anagram signal; H for hard comes from pencil grading. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is art or objects in poor, gaudy taste, which is tacky stuff.

clue.text: British flee in all directions, to village in part of Canada

indicators.note: in means the British and flee pieces sit inside the compass points

parts.note: the four compass points north, east, west and south give these letters
to flee is to run away
wick is an old word for a village, surviving in place names

explanation.surface: British people fleeing everywhere to a small village in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in all directions' looks like an anagram signal but gives the four compass points; 'in' is the container signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: New Brunswick is one of Canada's Maritime provinces, so it is a part of the country.

clue.text: Players picked for defending champions

definitions.meaning: in football or rugby the defensive players are the full-... and half-...
as a verb, one who champions a cause supports it

explanation.surface: Selecting players to defend a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenders in team sports are called by this name, and supports or champions is its verb sense.

clue.text: Finish off Guardian, for example, in Irish house

indicators.note: finish off means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: The Guardian is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Putting an end to the Guardian newspaper in the Irish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil Éireann is the lower chamber of Ireland's parliament, so it is an Irish house.

clue.text: Bird turned over eggs etc when disturbed

indicators.note: turned over says the word is read backwards

parts.note: ova is Latin for eggs

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of etc are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bird flipped its eggs and other things when frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' gives AVO from OVA; 'when disturbed' makes CET from ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with a long upcurved bill.

clue.text: Showing some Picasso on a screen, once

indicators.note: Showing some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Picasso painting displayed on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: As soon as and once both mean at the moment that, as in 'once he arrives'.

clue.text: Takes chair, as 'e's surrounded by lots of lions

indicators.note: surrounded by means the letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: groups of lions are called prides
the clue spells out the letters E and S as written

explanation.surface: A Cockney chairman, surrounded by lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e's is a Cockney-style 'he's', written as E and S; they go inside PRIDES: PR-ES-IDES. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair a meeting, so takes chair means the same.

clue.text: Title holder uses it

definitions.meaning: a name or nickname, as in informal usage for what someone is called
the part of a cup, door or tool that is gripped by the person holding it

explanation.surface: A titleholder making use of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word for a person's name or title, and it is also the grip by which an object is held.
